ideation.icp_description: B2B companies (all-sector, per user decision 2026-05-27), 100-1000 employees, HQ in US or UK, direct employers, that are HIRING SDR / BDR / Account Executive roles. The hire signals the company is scaling its sales team — more reps to onboard onto the tool stack.
ideation.offer: Arnic increases adoption of tools among a company's employees — gets the sales team to actually USE the sales stack they've bought. The person we email is the Head of Sales / VP Sales / CRO who owns the number.
ideation.why_signal_fits: A wave of new sales reps is exactly when tool adoption is won or lost — new hires either ramp on the stack from day one or never adopt it. Arnic ensures new reps actually use the tools as they onboard.
ideation._signal_strength_caveat: WEAK SIGNAL — user accepted BUILD-AS-IS on 2026-05-27 after two explicit flags. 'Hiring a rep' indicates a sales team exists, not specifically a tool-adoption problem. Filter kept raw including 'Account Executive' (a catch-all that TheirStack substring-matches into advertising/PR/insurance account-management roles). Heavy reliance on the role-qualification layer to screen noise downstream.

qualification._status: DRAFT — co-draft and confirm with user before go-live. EXTRA IMPORTANT for this brief since the filter is intentionally broad (build-as-is) — this layer does the heavy lifting on noise.
qualification._purpose: Role-only judgement layer applied by lilly-theirstack-data-processing Phase 2.5. Classifies each new Jobs row QUALIFIED / BORDERLINE / OFF_BRIEF on whether the hire is a genuine outbound sales-rep hire (= a new person who will need to adopt the sales stack). Never excludes companies — only roles.
qualification.role_signal_definition: The new hire is a quota-carrying outbound/inbound sales rep (SDR, BDR, Account Executive) who will onboard onto and use the company's sales tech stack. NOT a client-service 'account executive' (advertising/PR/media/insurance account management), not an account manager, not a partnerships or recruiting role.
qualified_role_patterns: Sales Development Representative / SDR / Outbound SDR / Inbound SDR
Business Development Representative / BDR / Account Development Representative / ADR
Account Executive where clearly a quota-carrying sales rep (SaaS/tech AE, Mid-Market AE, Enterprise AE, SMB AE)
disqualified_role_patterns: Advertising / PR / Media / Marketing 'Account Executive' — client-service / account-management, not a sales rep
Insurance Account Executive / Benefits Account Executive — book-of-business account manager
Account Manager / Client Manager / Customer Success — retention, not new-logo selling
Partnerships / Channel BDR / Partner Development — partner motion, not direct outbound
Recruiter / Talent / Sales Recruiter — internal hiring role
Intern / Junior / Trainee / Apprentice / Graduate-scheme level
borderline_role_patterns: Bare 'Account Executive' with no qualifier — could be a sales rep OR an account manager; check company context
'Business Development' without 'Representative' — could be partnerships rather than outbound sales
Senior Account Executive at <30 emp — could be a retitled IC or a player-coach

Role.instructions: Direct lookup from the Jobs row 'Job Title', NORMALISED so it reads naturally after the hardcoded hook 'Saw you're hiring a ___'. Rules: (1) replace a comma separating a level word from a function area with ' of ' so 'Director, Revenue Operations' becomes 'Director of Revenue Operations'; (2) drop bracketed/parenthetical or trailing geographic qualifiers so 'Sales Development Representative (Southeast)' becomes 'Sales Development Representative' and 'Account Executive - France & Southern Europe' becomes 'Account Executive'; (3) trim whitespace; (4) preserve seniority words (Senior, Director, Manager, Head, VP, Lead, Chief). No LLM call needed for (1)-(3); escalate only if genuinely ambiguous.
Role.validation: Non-empty. Reads naturally after 'Saw you're hiring a ___'. No comma in the level/function position, no parentheses, no trailing geographic qualifier.
